newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-TRAINER WILLIAMS SETS UP AUSTRALIAN WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TRAINER WILLIAMS SETS UP AUSTRALIAN WIN.

text.p: Trainer Dirk Williams, drafted into the injury-hit Australian side, scored the opening try as the Wallabies beat Scottish Districts 25-9 in miserable conditions at McDiarmid Park on Tuesday.
With Australia trailing 6-0 from two penalties eight minutes from halftime, Williams, playing at lock, touched down after a series of drives by the Wallaby forwards.
Just on half-time, fly-half Tim Wallace, who had earlier failed with two penalty attempts, succeeded with his third to put Australia ahead for the first time and earn them an 8-6 interval lead.

Districts, who kicked away much of their possession, went further behind three minutes into the second half when centre Adam Magro weaved his way through a splintered defence for the Wallabies' second try which Wallace converted.

Australia scored their third try when Districts full-back Gavin Fraser, attempting to trap a high ball with his foot, kicked it straight to Joe Roff and the strong-running winger made full use of the gift to register Australia's third try.
Australia were forced to call on Williams after a series of injuries depleted their squad.

Lock Garrick Morgan has already gone home with a broken ankle, flanker Michael Brial is another long-term casualty and centre Jason Little will be missing from Saturday's test against Scotland at Murrayfield.
